==English==
{{was wotd|2025|September|22}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵʰéysd-}}
The {{lg|noun}} is derived from {{inh|en|enm|gost}}, from {{inh|en|ang|gāst}}, {{m|ang|gǣst|t=breath, spirit, soul, ghost}} (compare modern {{cog|en|Holy Ghost}}), from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*gaist}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*gaistaz}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*ǵʰéysdos}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*ǵʰéysd-|t=anger, agitation}}.<ref name="OED">Compare {{R:OED Online|pos=n.'' and ''adj|id=6509148342|date=September 2025|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=n}}</ref>

The ''h'' in the spelling appears in the Prologue to {{w|William Caxton}}’s ''Royal Book'', printed in 1484, in a reference to the “[[Holy Ghost|Holy Ghoost]]”. It was likely influenced by {{cog|dum|gheest}}, a common variant of {{m|dum|geest}}. Both Caxton and his assistant {{w|Wynkyn de Worde}} had connections to the Low Countries.<ref name="OED"/><ref>{{cite-book|author=w:David Crystal|title=Spell It Out: The Singular Story of English Spelling|location=London|publisher=Profile Books|year=2012|isbn=978-1-84668-567-5}}</ref> {{doublet|en|geist}}.

The {{lg|adjective}} and {{lg|verb}}<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=1999598935|date=March 2025|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=v}}</ref> are derived from the noun. The verb gained prominence in the 2010s.<ref>{{cite-web |en |url=https://www.npr.org/2025/10/22/nx-s1-5580542/ghost-etymology-halloween-spooky-season |work=Word of the Week |publisher={{w|NPR}} |accessdate=2025-10-23 |date=2025-10-22 |title=The not-so-spooky origins of 'ghost' — and why the word still haunts our language |first=Joe |last=Hernandez|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251128145554/https://www.npr.org/2025/10/22/nx-s1-5580542/ghost-etymology-halloween-spooky-season|archivedate=28 November 2025}}</ref>

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# A [[disembodied]] [[soul]]; a soul or [[spirit]] of a [[deceased]] [[person]]; a spirit [[appear]]ing [[after]] [[death]].
#: {{synonyms|en|apparition|bogey|phantom|revenant|specter|spook|Thesaurus:ghost}}
#: {{ux|en|Everyone believed that the '''ghost''' of an old lady haunted the crypt.}}
#: {{ux|en|He believes in '''ghosts'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Dryden Annus Mirabilis|passage=The mighty '''ghosts''' of our great Harries rose.}}
#* {{RQ:Haggard She|passage=For a moment I was puzzled, but presently, of course, it struck me that he must have seen Ayesha, wrapped in her grave-like garment, and been deceived by the extraordinary undulating smoothness of her walk into a belief that she was a white '''ghost''' gliding towards him.}}
#* {{RQ:Schuster Hepaticae|volume=V|page=vii|passage=Hepaticology, outside the temperate parts of the Northern Hemisphere, still lies deep in the shadow cast by that ultimate "closet taxonomist," Franz Stephani—a '''ghost''' whose shadow falls over us all.}}
# {{lb|en|Christianity|literary|chiefly|archaic}} A [[spirit]]; a human [[soul]].
#: {{synonyms|en|essence|soul|spirit|anima|Thesaurus:ghost}}
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=I|canto=VII|stanza=31|passage=hen gins her grieued '''ghost''' thus to lament and mourne.}}
# {{lb|en|by extension}} Any faint shadowy semblance; an unsubstantial image.
#: {{synonyms|en|glimmer|glimmering|glimpse|hint|inkling|phantom|spark|suggestion}}
#: {{ux|en|not a '''ghost''' of a chance}}
#: {{ux|en|the '''ghost''' of an idea}}
#* {{RQ:Poe Raven|passage=And each separate dying ember wrought its '''ghost''' upon the floor.}}
#* {{quote-journal|1=en|date=July 23, 2017|author=Brandon Nowalk|title=The great game begins with a bang on Game Of Thrones (newbies)|work=The Onion AV Club|url=http://www.avclub.com/tvclub/great-game-begins-bang-game-thrones-newbies-258485|passage={{...|The Arya subplot makes up for a lot, though. At first she’s so aloof as to make you wonder whether there is any of the old Arya in there. She’s sitting there with her old friend Hot Pie, gorging on freshly baked bread, and she’s stuck in a terrible monotone.}} She barely answers his questions. She’s a '''ghost''' of herself. And then Hot Pie gives us the key to Arya’s whole thing this season so far: She didn’t know that Jon had defeated the Boltons.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170726230626/http://www.avclub.com/tvclub/great-game-begins-bang-game-thrones-newbies-258485|archivedate=26 July 2017}}

#: {{synonyms|en|echo}}
# {{lb|en|cleaning|graffiti slang}} A faint image that remains after an attempt to remove [[graffiti]].
#: {{synonyms|en|shadow}}
# {{lb|en|writing}} {{ellipsis of|en|ghostwriter}}.
#: {{ux|en|I’ve written both as a '''ghost''' for experts and under my name.}}
# A [[nonexistent]] person invented to obtain some (typically [[fraudulent]]) [[benefit]].
#*: Before filling out this form, please visit the Pennsic Pre-Registration Page to create your account and enter your campers and '''ghosts''' <!--explanatory gloss, not part of the original text-->[{{n-g|nonexistent campers one pays for to legitimately increase the size of one's allotted camping space}}].
# A [[dead]] person whose [[identity]] is stolen by another {{gl|see {{m|en|ghosting}}}}. {{rfv-sense|en}}
# {{lb|en|Internet}} An unresponsive user on [[IRC]], resulting from the user's [[client]] disconnecting without notifying the [[server]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|author=Paul Mutton|title=IRC Hacks: 100 Industrial-Strength Tips & Tools|page=31|passage=This will let you open a query with NickServ again so you can remove your “'''ghost'''” from the server: {{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|computing}} A [[copy]] of a [[file]] or [[record]].
#: {{synonyms|en|backup}}
# {{lb|en|theatre}} An [[understudy]]. {{rfv-sense|en}}
# {{lb|en|espionage}} A [[covert]] (and [[deniable]]) agent.
#: {{synonyms|en|spook|spy}}
# {{lb|en|video games}} An [[opponent]] in a [[race|racing]] [[game]] that follows a previously [[record]]ed [[route]], allowing players to compete against previous best times.
# Someone whose [[identity]] cannot be established because there are no records of such a  person.
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2014-08-19|author=Michael Sloan|title=The Equalizer: A Novel|publisher=Macmillan|isbn=9781250041968|page=156
|text="{{...}}no record of a Robert, or Bobby, Maclain that fits our man's description," Kuzbec said. "No social, no driver's license, no address, no military service record. He's a '''ghost'''." Kirov did find that interesting.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2015-11-03|author=Sherrilyn Kenyon|title=Born of Betrayal: The League: Nemesis Rising|publisher=St. Martin's Press|isbn=9781466840959
|text="He's a ghost. No record of any kind, anywhere. I got nothing when I did a trace. I'm thinking he was either erased or he's something we don't know about." Nyk rubbed at his jaw. "If he was erased, Syn, he'd have a record{{nb...}}"}}
# {{lb|en|quantum physics}} An [[unphysical]] [[state]] in a [[gauge theory]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1966|author=Kàzmèr L. Nagy|title=State Vector Spaces with Indefinite Metric in Quantum Field Theory|page=14|passage=The proof is well known, and independent of the metric, but to make certain we prove it here also for the case when the state vector system of an operator contains multipole{{sic}} '''ghosts'''.}}
# {{lb|en|computing|linguistics|attributive}} A formerly [[nonexistent]] [[character]] that was at some point [[mistaken]]ly [[encoded]] into a [[character set]] [[standard]], which might have since become used [[opportunistic]]ally for some [[genuine]] purpose.
#: {{ux|en|{{m|ja|彁}} is a '''ghost''' character from the Japanese JIS X 0208 character set.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} {{ellipsis of|en|ghost pepper}}.
# {{lb|en|uncountable|often capitalized}} A game in which players take turns to add a [[letter]] to a possible word, trying not to complete a word.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1897|author=Emma J. Gray|title=Fun for the Household: A Book of Games|page=110
|text='''GHOST.''' This is a spelling game. A person gives a letter, {{...}} his next neighbor must think of a word beginning with this letter, and then say the second letter, {{...}} }}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2008|month=04|author=Joanne O'Sullivan|title=I Don't Care If We're There Yet: The Backseat Boredom Buster|publisher=Lark Books|isbn=9781579908485|page=183
|text={{...}}word is, you win the round. But be warned : if she does have a real word in mind, you lose. Bluffing[:] It's possible to bluff in '''Ghost'''. For example, you can pretend to add a suffix to a word, even if that word doesn't exist. If no{{nb...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2013-07-17|author=Milton Pashcow|title=Sicilian Escapade: A Devil in Eden|publisher=Xlibris Corporation|isbn=9781483659725|page=21
|text={{...}}played '''ghost''', which was a popular word game at that time. '''Ghost''' was a very convenient game since it required no props, lights, or space. Each player must add a letter to the continuous formation of a word supplied by the previous player{{nb...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2018-06-12|author=Edward M. Hallowell|title=Because I Come from a Crazy Family: The Making of a Psychiatrist|publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing USA|isbn=9781632868602|page=26
|text={{...}}played '''ghost''', a word game. For quite a while, I spent most of my time at their house. I can't remember why I lived with them or exactly where my mother and my older brothers, Ben and John, were after Dad left.{{nb...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2017-11-01|author=Heidi Harley|title=English Words: A Linguistic Introduction|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=9781119485674
|text=Another game in which your phonotactic instincts are brought to bear is "Ghost," a good car game for spelling geeks. In '''Ghost''', players take turns adding a letter to a string of letters. The letter added must create the beginning of a correctly spelled word, but you don't want to add a letter which will complete{{nb...}}}}

### Of a [[disembodied#Adjective|disembodied]] [[soul#Noun|soul]]: to appear (somewhere or to someone) in the [[form#Noun|form]] of an [[apparition]]; to [[haunt#Verb|haunt]].

### To [[imbue]] (something) with a [[ghostlike|ghost-like]] [[effect#Noun|effect]] or [[hue]].
###* {{RQ:Lindsay Age of Consent|year=1962|page=32|passage=It spread slowly up from the sea-rim, a welling upwards of pure white light, '''ghosting''' the beach with silver and drawing the grey bastions of sandstone out of formless space.}}
## {{lb|en|by extension|figurative}}
### To [[continuously]] [[cause#Verb|cause]] (someone or something) [[trouble#Verb|trouble]]; specifically, to continuously be in the [[thought#Noun|thoughts]] of (someone) in a [[disturbing#Adjective|disturbing]] [[manner#Noun|manner]]; to [[perturb]], to [[trouble#Verb|trouble]].
### {{lb|en|slang}} To [[kill#Verb|kill]] (someone).
###* {{quote-av|en|date=2017-09-28|author=Josh Corbin|actor=Edi Gathegi|role=Ronald Dacey|title=Start Up|season=2|number=6|time=37:03|passage=RONALD: ”They tried to '''ghost''' your girl Isabel right here”. #### {{lb|en|graphical user interface}} To [[gray out]] (a [[visual#Adjective|visual]] [[element#Noun|element]]) to [[indicate]] that it is [[unavailable#Adjective|unavailable]].
#### {{lb|en|Internet}} To [[forcibly]] [[disconnect#Verb|disconnect]] (an [[IRC]] [[user]]) who is [[use#Verb|using]] one's [[reserved#Adjective|reserved]] [[nickname#Noun|nickname]].
### {{lb|en|chiefly|social media|slang}} To [[stop#Verb|stop]] [[communicate#Verb|communicating]] with (someone) on [[social media]], through [[text message]]s, etc., without [[explanation]], especially as a [[way#Noun|way]] of [[end#Verb|ending]] a [[relationship]]; hence, to end a relationship with (someone) by stopping all [[communication]] without explanation.
###* {{RQ:Guardian|date=15 October 2015|title=Why is it so hard to go from chatting on Tinder to meeting up in real life?|url=http://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2015/oct/15/swipe-right-ask-eva-tinder-meeting-in-real-life|passage=I've recently been trying out Tinder, and while I match with people and even chat with them everything seems to be going well, but whenever I bring up meeting IRL, they are quick to '''ghost''' me.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160824122124/https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2015/oct/15/swipe-right-ask-eva-tinder-meeting-in-real-life}}

### {{lb|en|chiefly|UK|law enforcement}} To [[transfer#Verb|transfer]] (a [[prisoner]]) to another [[prison#Noun|prison]], usually without [[first#Adverb|first]] [[inform#Verb|informing]] the prisoner.
## {{synonym of|en|ghostwrite|t=to [[write#Verb|write]] (a [[literary]] [[work#Noun|work]] or [[speech#Noun|speech]]), or [[produce#Verb|produce]] (an [[artistic#Adjective|artistic]] work)), in the [[place#Noun|place]] of someone}}; also, to [[carry out]] (an artistic [[performance]]) in the place of someone.
##* {{RQ:Bellow Humboldt's Gift|year=1976|page=41|passage=Well, you wrote a few books, you wrote a famous play, and even that was half '''ghosted'''.}}
